beats.subline: Friday, October 23, 2026 close — Thursday's tech-driven AI-spending selloff spread into other sectors, pulling the Dow down over 1% as oil jumped on Mideast tensions.
beats.body: Consumer and healthcare stocks led broader declines even as some chipmakers rebounded; WTI crude topped $100 a barrel on fears of renewed US-Iran escalation, and cybersecurity shares such as CrowdStrike gained after a critical PHP vulnerability disrupted government websites across Europe.

beats.headline: Trump claims US control of Strait of Hormuz as oil hits five-month high before midterms
beats.body: At a Friday rally, Trump said the Strait of Hormuz is "totally ours" and that the US could seize Iran's oil fields or "the whole country," as Brent crude settled above $116 a barrel on renewed Mideast escalation fears; separately, IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said the agency is ready to resume monitoring Iran's nuclear program if a diplomatic deal is reached, and Putin is set to host Iran's president in Moscow next week.

beats.headline: No fresh news on this beat right now
beats.body: The most substantive items this week — China's sovereignty claim over the Pratas Islands and Taiwan's report of 27 PLA aircraft near the island — fall outside the 72-hour window or were already covered in prior briefs, and no qualifying new development surfaced today.

beats.headline: Netanyahu says he's ordered Israel to work toward toppling Iran's regime; Trump threatens new strikes
beats.body: Netanyahu said he directed the IDF, Mossad and other security agencies to pursue the overthrow of Iran's government, calling it the only way to permanently end the nuclear threat, and said Trump has told him the US is "ready to finish the job" alongside Israel; at a Friday rally, Trump said the US could launch "another little epic fury" if Tehran doesn't agree to US terms.

beats.headline: Pentagon and Lockheed agree to 10-year framework for at least 850 F-35s
beats.body: The framework announced Thursday would lock in roughly 85 US F-35 purchases a year for a decade, with Lockheed self-funding at least $7 billion in program initiatives, but it can't become a binding contract until Congress passes a full defense bill authorizing multiyear buys — something Senate Democrats have delayed until after the midterms.

beats.headline: Anthropic merges Claude Chat and Cowork into one enterprise experience
beats.body: Anthropic said enterprise-plan subscribers now get a single unified Claude experience spanning chat and Cowork's multi-step task features across web, desktop and mobile, following last week's Claude Duet agent preview for Pro and Max subscribers.

beats.headline: Bears TE Cole Kmet out for the season, headed to injured reserve
beats.body: Head coach Ben Johnson confirmed Friday that Kmet will go on injured reserve for the rest of 2026 because of a right knee injury suffered in Thursday night's game against New England; with the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching, Chicago must now lean more heavily on tight ends Colston Loveland and Sam Roush.
